scenes.title: Add Calls Summary to the training board

captions.text: Calls Summary gives a supervisor a compact view of the
department's active-call workload.
In the open Add Widget panel, choose Calls Summary.
This example uses four fictional calls and the department's Routine,
Urgent and Emergency priorities.
A shared display can help the coordination team notice workload, then
turn to the detailed calls list for the incident names and assignments.
Use a training department when practicing changes to the board.
Use the gear icon at the upper right to open configuration,
then select Calls Summary Widget.
Keep Show Recent Call and Show Priority Counts on.
Set Max Priorities to Show to All.

spoken_references.Max Priorities to Show: All: Max Priorities to Show to All

captions.text: This first view uses Font Size at fourteen points, width four
and height three grid units.
Select Save and scroll to the summary.
Giving the panel enough room keeps the recent-call card and
priority rows readable together.

scenes.title: Compare the summary with the detailed calls

captions.text: The summary shows Active four, Routine three, Urgent one and Emergency zero.
Its recent-call card displays the fictional scheduled community
standby that was already dispatched during an earlier exercise.
The date in its name is a historical training label.
Scroll to the detailed Calls table and compare the Priority
column: three rows are Routine, and the warehouse alarm is Urgent.
A priority count summarizes calls; it does not identify which people
or units are available to respond.

scenes.title: Limit visible priority rows without filtering active calls

captions.text: Return to Calls Summary Widget and change Max Priorities to Show to one.

spoken_references.Max Priorities to Show: 1: Max Priorities to Show to one

captions.text: Select Save and inspect the board again.
Only the Routine row, with three calls, remains in the priority section.
Active still shows four.
This option limits how many priority rows the panel displays; it does not close,
remove or filter the underlying calls.
A restricted display can therefore omit an urgent category even while its
call still contributes to the total.

scenes.title: Show counts without the recent-call card

captions.text: For a count-focused display, return Max Priorities to Show to
All, turn Show Recent Call off and keep Show Priority Counts on.
Increase Font Size to sixteen points, then select Save.
The board now shows Active four and all three priority rows without the
recent-call name and address card.
This changes the summary presentation.
The detailed calls remain available elsewhere on the board.
Choose a text size that people can read from the actual viewing distance.

scenes.title: Use a minimal total and understand its limits

captions.text: Turn Show Priority Counts off as well and select Save.
With both optional sections hidden, the Calls panel contains just Active four.
The compact total may suit a secondary display, but viewers
can no longer see the workload's priority distribution in that panel.
Hiding information does not make its underlying incidents disappear.
Decide what your coordination team needs to see before adopting this minimal view.

scenes.title: Restore the full view and check saved preferences

captions.text: Restore Show Recent Call and Show Priority Counts, leave Max Priorities
to Show at All, and select Save.
Reload the board and inspect the complete summary again.
Active remains four, with Routine three, Urgent one and Emergency zero.
Reopen Calls Summary Widget to read back both enabled switches, All, Font Size
sixteen and the four-by-three dimensions.
Checking the saved controls as well as the visible result confirms the configuration
the display is actually using.

scenes.title: Apply the same display choices across organizations

captions.text: These display choices also fit departments beyond fire and E M S.
Security teams can summarize service calls and patrol incidents.
Search-and-rescue coordinators can monitor their mission workload.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams, wildland
contractors and industrial emergency response teams can use their own
call priorities in the same way.
Keep the full category view when every priority matters, and
consult the detailed Calls table when a count needs investigation.
